title: What If You Could Do Anything You've Watched on YouTube?

facts.claim: YouTube viewers watch over 1 billion hours of video a day
facts.source: YouTube announcement, Feb 2017 (Cristos Goodrow), reported by Engadget, The Next Web, 9to5Google

facts.claim: Viewers watch on average less than a quarter of a video (23.7% average retention across 10,000+ videos)
facts.source: Retention Rabbit 2025 benchmark, cited by vidIQ / Subscribr; a vendor benchmark, not an official YouTube figure

facts.claim: Magnus Carlsen has been world number 1 since July 2011; peak rating 2882 (May 2014) is the highest in history
facts.source: FIDE rating lists; Wikipedia 'Magnus Carlsen'; Chess.com

facts.claim: Park chess hustlers play for about $5 to $20 a game
facts.source: ChessBase (Maurice Ashley); Baruch College journalism blog; Chess.com blog

facts.claim: Magnus Carlsen played the chess hustlers in Washington Square Park in 2016
facts.source: Stabroek News, 'Carlsen schools chess hustlers in Washington Square Park', Oct 2016

facts.claim: Average homeowners water damage/freezing claim is about $15,400 (2019-2023)
facts.source: Insurance Information Institute (Triple-I), via Insurance Business Magazine / This Old House

facts.claim: In May 2022 a passenger with no flying experience landed a Cessna 208 at Palm Beach after the pilot became incapacitated, talked down by controller Robert Morgan, a flight instructor

lines.text: You're juggling 5 kitchen knives, and you have never juggled before. In 3 seconds, you'll find out why that's a problem.
At exactly 38 seconds, your hands just stop.
Bro! You almost lost a finger!
I stopped the video at 38 seconds!
Because this morning, you woke up able to do everything you have ever watched on YouTube. Up to the exact second you stopped watching.
In the next 30 days, you'll beat a chess hustler with moves from the best player alive, fill your garage with 11 chairs nobody wants, flood your kitchen, and land a plane. Almost.
Here's how it works. Every video in your watch history, you can now do. Cooking. Card tricks. Guitar. Backflips.
But only up to the second you clicked away. And your history froze this morning. Anything you watch from now on doesn't count.
YouTube says people watch over 1 billion hours of video every day. And one study of more than 10,000 videos found that viewers watch, on average, less than a quarter of each one.
Which means you have a lot of half skills.
Guitar? The first 40 seconds of one song. Backflips? You know the jump. Not the landing.
And one video from 3 a.m. last March. How to land a plane in an emergency. 71 percent watched.
You fell asleep again. The end was the best part.
Remember that.
There's just one problem. You got fired on Monday. Rent is 1,400 dollars, due on the 1st. You have 210 dollars.
The 1st. Not the 2nd. Not I'm almost there. The 1st.
30 days. Time to make money with your half skills.
Day 2. Theo films you trying a backflip in the backyard.
You nail the jump. You do not nail the landing.
2 million views, bro! We're rich!
You are not rich. You watched 9 percent of How to make money on YouTube. You never turned on ads.
Plan A. Everybody has seen this video. How I make 5,000 dollars a month flipping furniture. You watched 62 percent of it.
So you can find the chair. Haggle the price. Sand it, stain it, polish it. It looks better than new.
The part about how to sell it was in the other 38 percent.
By day 6, there are 11 beautiful chairs in your garage. Nobody has bought one.
Do the thing from the video!
There is no more video, Theo!
You spent 170 dollars on chairs. You've sold zero. You have 40 dollars left.
Plan B. You scroll through your history again. And there it is. 400 hours of Magnus Carlsen.
He's been the world number 1 since 2011. His peak rating, 2882, is the highest in chess history.
And you watched every single game to the end. Over breakfast. For 3 years.
Day 8. The park. The chess hustlers here play for 5 to 20 dollars a game.
Five bucks. Three minutes. Sit down, kid.
41 seconds later, he is staring at the board like it insulted his mother.
Again. Double or nothing.
You win 9 in a row. He has never lost 9 in a row. To anyone.
Who taught you to play like that?
Magnus. Sort of.
In 2016, Magnus Carlsen really did sit down with the chess hustlers in Washington Square Park in New York. They lost too.
By day 15, you have a regular table, 900 dollars, and a manager.
Twenty-five percent. And I bring the coffee.
But half skills are dangerous.
Day 17. The kitchen sink is leaking. You watched a plumbing video once. You stopped right before he said, first, turn off the water.
The Insurance Information Institute says the average water damage claim is about 15,000 dollars.
Yours is only 860. Which is all of your money.
Do you want me to watch the rest of it?
It doesn't count anymore!
Day 20. 40 dollars. 11 days left. And 11 chairs.
Wait. My uncle Ray just opened an office. He needs chairs. Like, 11 chairs.
Uncle Ray flies tourists around in a small plane. He'll buy all 11. But first, he wants to meet you. At the airfield.
Nice chairs. Want a ride before I pay you?
You check your history. How to land a plane in an emergency. 71 percent.
What could go wrong?
Day 29. 3,000 feet up. The view is incredible. Then Uncle Ray goes very quiet.
I don't feel so... great.
And he slumps over the controls.
Do the thing from the video! Do the thing!
And for the first time, the thing from the video is exactly what you need. You know the radio. You know the words.
Mayday, mayday. The pilot is unconscious. I'm a passenger.
Copy that. Stay calm, you're doing great. Do you have any flying experience?
About 6 minutes of a YouTube video.

It has happened for real. In 2022, a passenger with no flying experience landed a plane in Florida after the pilot passed out. An air traffic controller, who was also a flight instructor, talked him down.
You line up with the runway. Speed, perfect. Flaps, perfect. 500 feet. 300. 100.
And then your hands stop. 71 percent. This is where you fell asleep.
Theo! How does it end?!
Power to idle! Pull back slowly! Nose up! Let it float! I watched the end! You were snoring!
You pull back. The nose comes up. The wheels touch. One little bounce. Then just the sound of the runway.
Welcome back to the ground. Nice landing.
Uncle Ray is fine. Low blood sugar. He pays for all 11 chairs, plus a bonus for not dying.
1,500 dollars. And you're never flying with me again.
Day 30. The rent is paid. On the 1st. With 140 dollars to spare.
Huh. The 1st.
Turns out every video you fell asleep to, Theo watched the ending. You had the hands. He had the ending.
Okay. Now do the thing from my history.
Theo's history is 1,200 hours of people cutting soap. And one video. How to tell your best friend you scratched his car.
Theo?
Do you want me to watch the end?
That night, your phone buzzes. There's a new video in your history. You never clicked it.
How to perform surgery. 4 percent watched.
And somebody is knocking on your door.
So if you could do everything you've ever watched, which video would you finish first? Tell us in the comments.
